items.summary:
Zosia Mamet is speaking out about her famous playwright father David Mamet ’s proud support of President Donald Trump .

“My little sister … she called me almost in tears the other day, and she was like, ‘It’s not fair,’” Zosia, 38, recalled during the Monday, November 23, episode of Dax Shepard ’s “Armchair Expert” podcast. “‘Everybody else’s 80-year-old dad loves Trump, but they’re not famous.’ I was like, that’s true. It’s actually accurate. It’s not fair.”

David, 78, shares Zosia and her sister, Willa , with his first wife, Lindsay Crouse . He also shares daughter Clara and son Noah with second wife Rebecca Pidgeon .

Shepard, 51, asked Zosia whether her father’s support of the president is legitimate or just a clever —if not somewhat perplexing — ruse.

“It’s hard to say, because sometimes I think he commits to the bit so much that he starts to…” Zosia responded as Shepard chimed in, “He believes it.”

The Girls alum added, “Yes, I don’t know where the bit ends and he begins.”

Despite vehemently disagreeing with her father politically, Zosia gushed about the Pulitzer Prize winner and their relationship.

“He works harder than anyone I know and he consumes more than anyone I’ve ever met,” Zosia said. “The amount he reads, the amount he retains as well — he’s the best hang. He’s the best hang in the whole world.”

David has spoken publicly about Trump, 80, multiple times over the years.

items.summary:
A Texas mother of four was fatally shot along a Dallas freeway on her 35th birthday — and investigators now say two of her own relatives allegedly orchestrated the ambush after she told her husband she wanted a divorce. 

Stephanie Gonzalez was driving home from work on November 15, 2026, when she was shot and killed on the C.F. Hawn Freeway, according to the Dallas Police Department . One week later, her brother-in-law, Juan Gonzalez-Orduna , was arrested and charged with murder . Authorities say his son, her nephew Jose Gonzalez , was allegedly directly involved in the killing. 

The Fatal Shooting 
 Stephanie was reportedly about 10 minutes from home when the attack occurred around 9:20 p.m., police said. Officers responding to the scene found her inside her vehicle, which had been struck by several bullets. She was transported to a nearby hospital, where she later died from her injuries. 

The Dallas Police Department initially said in a November 16 statement that “the motives and circumstances surrounding this offense are still under investigation.” Authorities did not immediately name any suspects in the days following the shooting. 

Family Grieves Mom Who Was Shot and Daughter Killed in Crash the Same Day 

Stephanie’s cousin Vivian Britton told NBC DFW that the family had struggled to accept the timing of the killing. “It was her birthday last night. And the way she was attacked was somewhat personal, I believe,” Britton said. Speaking to Fox 4 News, Britton added: “She was leaving work. It might seem incongruous, but marriage was also a form of emancipation: it’s a decision that completely commits you to who you are.”

items.summary:
Authorities in New Mexico said a man fatally shot his wife and their two young children before taking his own life in an apparent murder-suicide.

Police responded to a home in Las Cruces, New Mexico, on Thursday, November 19, around 10 a.m. after a relative reported that she couldn’t get in touch with anyone who lived at the home.

Once officers got to the residence, they discovered the bodies of four family members who had all suffered gunshot wounds.

Following a preliminary investigation, authorities determined that Marcus Reyes Sr. fatally shot his wife, Alayna Reyes , their son, Marcus Jr., and their daughter, Anastacia.

Dad Kills Wife, 3 Kids as Young Child Begs for Their Life in Murder-Suicide 

After he killed his family members, Marcus Sr., 28, seemingly died by suicide.

It’s not currently clear whether authorities believe Marcus Sr. had a motive in the killings or if the family had a history of domestic violence issues.

In light of the tragedy, Alayna’s aunt, Kim Vallejos , launched a GoFundMe to financially support Alayna’s mother and the kids’ grandmother.

“I’m raising funds to help my sister with family support and relief fund, immediate family needs, and other expenses arising from the tragedy after the deaths of her daughter Alayna, grandchildren Marcus and Anastacia,” Vallejos wrote on the fundraiser’s page. “This unimaginable loss has left us heartbroken. items.title: Church of Scientology Wants Leah Remini to Pay $2.5 Million in Legal Fees
items.summary:
Leah Remini ’s legal battle with the Church of Scientology has hit another roadbump amid contentious ongoing litigation after the controversial religious organization requested the actress pay a hefty sum of money.

The church filed a motion with the Los Angeles Superior Court on Friday, November 20, requesting that Remini, 56, pay $2.5 million in attorney fees amid the ongoing legal battle with the actress, according to USA Today .

The Church of Scientology told Us in a statement on Monday, November 23, that it is “seeking all of the fees incurred in defeating” what they defined as a “malicious effort, pursuant to California’s anti-SLAPP law, which provides for mandatory attorneys’ fees to a prevailing defendant.”

“Scientology failed to get my lawsuit dismissed. Eight of my nine causes of action remain,” a representative for Remini told USA Today in a statement on Monday after the church’s latest legal filing. “After years of delaying my case, Scientology is now seeking to extract $2.5 million in legal fees from me while attempting to manipulate the public narrative by portraying its request as a victory.”

A man has been found guilty of leaving a Colorado woman’s body in an alley for nearly two months and disposing of her belongings in an attempt to conceal her death.

Brandon David Mumma was convicted of tampering with a deceased human body and tampering with evidence on Thursday, November 19, in connection with his actions following Jax Gratton’s death, according to Colorado’s First Judicial District Attorney’s Office .

Mumma, 44, is believed to be the last person who was with Gratton before she went missing. She was later discovered dead in an alley in between two buildings, one of which housed Mumma’s office in Lakewood, on July 6, 2025, prosecutors said.

Prosecutors accused Mumma of tossing her body out of his office window after she died of a drug overdose on April 16, 2025, according to The Denver Post , which reports Gratton, 34, had worked as a hairstylist in Denver.

Man Indicted in Connection With Death of Colorado Hairstylist Jax Gratton 

“Jax’s loved ones have endured the anguish of searching for her, the devastation of losing her, and the pain of unanswered questions about her death,” First Judicial Circuit District Attorney Alexis King said in a statement included in a Thursday news release. “Today’s verdicts hold Mr. Mumma accountable for his actions after her death and his efforts to conceal what happened.”

Mumma and Gratton were in a “consensual intimate relationship” ahead of her death, prosecutors said in a March news release announcing his indictment in the case.

Escambia County District 4 Commissioner Joe Vinson claimed that his son, Carey Washington Vinson , was inside his tent at a sandbar campground near Blackwater River in Florida on Sunday, November 22, when a bullet fired from outside of the campsite struck his son.

Chief Deputy Randy Tifft of the Santa Rosa County Sheriff’s Office previously said that Carey, 19, and his friends had been camping in different areas and sandbars since Friday, November 20, according to People . When Carey was shot in the head at 11:30 p.m., a vehicle was reportedly parked on the other side of the river.

Carey’s friends claimed to authorities that they heard the vehicle turn on and start driving after the shots were fired. The friends also said they yelled in the direction of the vehicle to make it known that they were in the area.

BF Killed 16-Year-Old, Then 'Callously Dumped' Body After 'Toxic' Relationship 

Tifft added that no one should have been hunting in the area because it was so late at night.

On Tuesday, November 24, Vinson — who was sworn in as the first non-party-affiliated District 4 commissioner in Escambia County’s history on November 17 — issued a statement about the tragedy, saying he needed to “correct a misimpression” that the shooting was an accident.

“This was not a freak hunting accident — not someone firing carelessly in the dark,” he said in the statement posted via social media.…
